item.title: Of all the ways Chairman Kevin Warsh wants to remake the Fed, the least flashy may be the most lasting: He is cutting the number of interest-rate decisions the central bank makes each year
item.content:encoded: The Federal Reserve confirmed that it won’t vote on interest rates at its October meeting next year.

item.title: Canada Factory Activity Flatlines in September
item.content:encoded: Manufacturing activity stalled in September despite a tailwind from higher energy prices, signaling a weak end to the quarter as the industry struggles with trade tensions and heightened uncertainty.

item.title: It takes too long and costs too much to build big in the U.S., writes @greg_ip
item.content:encoded: Even with an AI boom, it still takes too long and costs too much to build big things in the U.S.

item.title: Week Ahead for FX, Bonds: Fed Minutes, U.K. Data in Focus
item.content:encoded: Market expectations for another Fed rate rise in December have increased in the wake of stronger-than-expected jobs data and higher-than-anticipated inflation.

item.title: New Zealand’s Jobless Rate Climbs Ahead Of Election
item.content:encoded: The unemployment rate rose to 5.7%, its highest level since mid-2015, defying expectations of a fall and affirming the central bank’s recent caution around raising interest rates further.

item.title: Home sales declined in October to their lowest level since 2010, a new trough for a housing market that has been hovering near rock bottom for more than four years
item.content:encoded: Sales of existing homes declined 5.5% from the previous month, dropping the level of sales to the lowest point since the subprime crisis period.

item.title: The U.S. is in a battle to lower the costs to build housing, but it’s losing—as factors including the Iran war and tariffs fuel rising expenses for home builders
item.content:encoded: The Iran war, tariffs and the AI build-out have pushed up the costs of materials, labor and borrowing.

item.title: U.S. Housing Starts Dropped Again in September
item.content:encoded: Housing starts fell 5.2% in September to 1.221 million. Economists had expected a reading of 1.3 million and for starts to rise 2% over the month.

item.title: Producer-Price Inflation Cooled Last Month, Remains Elevated
item.content:encoded: Prices charged by U.S. producers rose less quickly last month than during their rapid increase in September, but wholesale inflation over the past year remains well above trend.

item.title: Federal Reserve to Forgo Rate Decision at October 2027 Meeting
item.content:encoded: The central bank’s proposed schedule calls for eight meetings in 2027, as is typical, but notes that the meeting slated for late October will not include a policy decision.

item.title: Shoppers’ complaints about food prices could soon grow louder, as surging energy costs and supply-chain delays are elevating costs for producers: “The worst is yet to come”
item.content:encoded: Grocery prices could increase again as surging energy costs and supply-chain delays are lifting costs for producers.

item.title: U.S., Eurozone Bond Yields Rise
item.content:encoded: Bond yields rose in Europe and the U.S. as inflationary pressures kept expectations for further Federal Reserve interest-rate increases strong.

item.title: A Quarter of Key Goods Vulnerable to Supply Disruptions, Study Finds
item.content:encoded: The disruptions could have damaging consequences for the economies that import these key goods, according to a study by the McKinsey Global Institute.

item.title: Eurozone Retail Sales Slump as Energy Shock Hits Confidence
item.content:encoded: Retail sales fell in as high energy prices continued to weigh on consumer confidence.

item.title: U.S. Home Price Growth Kept Climbing in August
item.content:encoded: The S&P Cotality Case-Shiller National Home Price Index, which measures home prices across the country, rose 2.1% in the 12 months through August, compared with a 1.9% increase in July.

item.title: Treasury Selloff Accelerates, European Bonds Follow Suit
item.content:encoded: The selloff in Treasurys accelerated as Federal Reserve officials spoke about their path to lower inflation through higher interest rates.

item.title: Consumer Sentiment Declined Slightly in October
item.content:encoded: The University of Michigan survey’s headline index came in at 48, down from 48.1 in September and hovering near record-low levels.

item.title: Eurozone Goods-Trade Deficit Widens on Higher Energy Prices
item.content:encoded: The eurozone’s deficit in its trade in goods with the rest of the world continued to widen in September as households and businesses had to pay more for imports of fossil fuels.

item.title: German Trade Surplus Narrows Despite Rising Exports
item.content:encoded: German exports rebounded in September, offering some relief to manufacturers after a volatile summer, but faster growth in imports weighed on the country’s trade surplus.

item.title: Canada’s Trade Surplus Widens as Oil, Gold Drive Record Exports
item.content:encoded: The widening to C$5.35 billion in September marked the the biggest surplus in over four years as exports hit a fresh record high.
